title: Spring Boot Setup & Project Basics: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before notes on bootstrapping a Spring Boot app: Spring Initializr, Maven vs Gradle, the parent POM and starters, project layout, @SpringBootApplication, and running and packaging the app.

chapters.title: Spring Initializr and the Boot Mental Model
points: Spring Initializr (start.spring.io, or IDE wizard, or `curl https://start.spring.io/starter.zip`) generates a zipped skeleton: build file, main class, test class, application.properties, wrapper scripts
Boot = Spring + auto-configuration + starters + embedded server: it configures beans from the classpath so you write almost no XML or boilerplate
Initializr choices that matter: project type (Maven/Gradle), language, Boot version, group/artifact, packaging (jar/war), Java version, dependencies
Example CLI: `curl https://start.spring.io/starter.zip -d dependencies=web,data-jpa -d type=maven-project -d javaVersion=21 -o demo.zip`
Convention over configuration: sensible defaults (port 8080, embedded Tomcat, `application.properties`) that you override only when needed

chapters.title: Maven vs Gradle
points: Maven: XML `pom.xml`, fixed lifecycle (validate, compile, test, package, verify, install, deploy), convention-driven and declarative
Gradle: Groovy or Kotlin DSL `build.gradle(.kts)`, task graph, incremental builds and build cache, usually faster on big projects
Comparison row: Maven is stricter and more uniform; Gradle is more flexible and faster but easier to over-customize
Always run via the wrapper (`./mvnw`, `./gradlew`; `mvnw.cmd` / `gradlew.bat` on Windows) so everyone uses the same build tool version without installing it
Mistake: committing without the wrapper files, or mixing a globally installed `mvn`/`gradle` version with the project's wrapper

chapters.title: Parent POM, Dependency Management and Starters
points: `spring-boot-starter-parent` as `<parent>` supplies dependency-management (a BOM of tested versions), plugin config, Java version and UTF-8 defaults, and resource filtering
Because of the managed BOM, you declare dependencies WITHOUT `<version>`; overriding a version uses a property like `<spring-data-bom.version>` or an explicit `<version>`

No parent allowed (company parent POM)? import `spring-boot-dependencies` as a BOM in `<dependencyManagement>` with `<scope>import</scope>` and `<type>pom</type>`; Gradle uses the `io.spring.dependency-management` plugin
Starter = one curated dependency pulling a set of transitive libs: `spring-boot-starter-web` (MVC + Tomcat + Jackson), `-data-jpa`, `-test`, `-security`, `-validation`, `-actuator`
Mistake: pinning explicit versions of managed libs, which creates a mismatch with the Boot BOM; also adding a starter for every library instead of only what you need

chapters.title: Project Layout, Main Class and @SpringBootApplication
points: Standard layout: `src/main/java` (code), `src/main/resources` (`application.properties` or `.yml`, `static/`, `templates/`), `src/test/java` (tests)
Main class has `public static void main` calling `SpringApplication.run(DemoApplication.class, args)`, which creates the ApplicationContext, runs auto-configuration and starts the embedded server
`@SpringBootApplication` = `@SpringBootConfiguration` + `@EnableAutoConfiguration` + `@ComponentScan`
Component scan starts at the main class's package and covers its sub-packages only; place the main class in the root package (e.g. `com.example.demo`)
Mistake: a bean or controller in a sibling or parent package is never found, giving 404s or `NoSuchBeanDefinitionException`; fix by moving it or setting `scanBasePackages`

chapters.title: Running and Packaging the App
points: Run in dev: `./mvnw spring-boot:run` or `./gradlew bootRun`, or the IDE run button on the main class
Package: `./mvnw clean package` produces `target/demo-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar`; Gradle: `./gradlew bootJar` into `build/libs/`
Run the packaged app with `java -jar target/demo-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar`; override config with `--server.port=9090` or `SERVER_PORT=9090`
Executable fat jar (embedded server, nested libs via the `spring-boot-maven-plugin` / Boot Gradle plugin) vs war (needs an external servlet container; extend `SpringBootServletInitializer`)
Mistake: running `java -jar` on the plain jar when the Boot plugin is missing (`no main manifest attribute`), or port 8080 already in use (change `server.port`)

chapters.title: Spring Boot Setup Cheat Sheet
points: Bootstrap: start.spring.io, then pick build tool, Boot version, Java version, jar packaging and starters
Commands: `./mvnw spring-boot:run`, `./mvnw clean package`, `./gradlew bootRun`, `./gradlew bootJar`, `java -jar app.jar`
Parent POM or BOM manages versions, so omit `<version>` on starters and managed libs
`@SpringBootApplication` = configuration + auto-configuration + component scan from the main class's package down
Pitfalls: main class not in the root package, version overrides drifting from the BOM, missing wrapper files, port 8080 clash
